findings.rationale: Accepted: section 3b named the review and author files but not what has to be built inside each. Phase 3 now enumerates the per-rail responsibilities (binary init, the existing --bin override, command precondition, invocation, stdout/stderr capture, failure mapping into each script's existing classifier, and the codex mirror).

Accepted: --cursor-fast was added as a seam without appearing in the user-facing usage surfaces. It is now on the header usage sites and is runner-scoped - passing it with a non-cursor runner is a die_precondition, the same posture --endpoint already has for non-cc-shim runners.

Accepted and materially improves the design: validating against a different binary than the one that runs is exactly the class of bug --cursor-bin exists to make testable. The resolved binary is now an explicit first argument to cursor_model_for, so --list-models validation, execution, and the test seam all target the same binary.

Accepted: Phase 2 would have shipped a cursor runner that resolve-review-loop.sh rejects with exit 3. The contract enums base dispatch depends on (schema runner enum, readiness maps, the four roster allowlists, codex mirrors) move into Phase 2 with check-contract-schema.js and check-canonical-invariants.sh attached to that phase's acceptance; Phase 3 keeps only review/author-specific work.

Accepted - the same over-claim flagged in this session before dispatch and not fully removed. Priority lane, not a faster decoder was a mechanism claim n=3 cannot support. Restated as observation: the fast variants showed higher throughput and markedly less variable time-to-first-flush in this sample; a queueing explanation fits but is not established, and billing remains unknown.

Correct, and the sharpest finding of either generation: the generation-1 repair closed only the cursor- prefixed mis-route while section 1 names two, so gpt-5.3-codex-low still reached the codex rail untested. The guard now matches two classes - any cursor-* id, and any exact id in the Phase 1 table - and the negative-control test iterates the whole table, prefixed and non-prefixed. Ids outside that table stay out of scope with the reason recorded, so the guard is closed-world over what this plan enables.
